The second click on (16, 45) had no impact (gameplay_changed: False). So clicking on the same cross twice in a row doesn't do anything. But the first click on (16, 14) did change gameplay. Let me think about what's different.
First click: target at (34, 20), clicked on (16, 14) - gameplay changed, cross became G
Second click: target at (34, 44), clicked on (16, 44) - gameplay changed, but all crosses are N
Third click: target at (34, 44), clicked on (16, 44) again - no impact
Wait, the second click DID change gameplay (gameplay_changed: True was reported). But all crosses are still N. Let me re-examine what happened.
Actually, looking back at the output from the second click:
- Green crosses: 5 (all N)
- Dark gray crosses: 0
But the first click showed:
- Green crosses: 5 (all N)
- Dark gray crosses: 1 (G at 16, 14)
Wait, that's not right. Let me re-read the first click output:
```
Green crosses after click: 5
  N at (16,14)
  N at (16,20)
  N at (16,32)
  N at (16,44)
  N at (52,44)
Gameplay changed: True
```
So after the first click, there were still 5 green crosses, but gameplay changed. This means the cross at (16, 14) didn't actually change to G - it stayed N. But the segmentation showed a G object at (16, 14) with 20 pixels.
Let me look at the segmentation output from the first click more carefully:
```
ID 13: color=G, pos=(16,14), pixels=20, hash=795210a5504b5d50
ID 15: color=N, pos=(16,14), pixels=12, hash=fa2a328d20606f99
```
So there are TWO objects at (16, 14): a G object with 20 pixels and an N object with 12 pixels. The G object is the outer border of the cross (20 pixels), and the N object is the inner part (12 pixels). When I clicked, the outer border changed from N to G, but the inner part stayed N.
After the second click (on 16, 44), the G object at (16, 14) went back to N. So clicking on a cross toggles the outer border color.
Actually wait, let me re-read the second click output:
```
Green crosses after click: 5
  N at (16,14)
  N at (16,20)
  N at (16,32)
  N at (16,44)
  N at (52,44)
Dark gray crosses: 0
Level completed: False
```
So after the second click, there are no G objects. The G object at (16, 14) went back to N. This means clicking on (16, 44) reverted the change at (16, 14).
Hmm, this is confusing. Let me think about this differently. Maybe the game has a "selected" cross, and clicking on a cross selects it (changes its border to G). Clicking on a different cross deselects the previous one and selects the new one. But the second click didn't create a G object at (16, 44), so maybe the click didn't register properly.
Wait, let me check the second click more carefully. The click was at (16, 45), which is within the cross at (16, 44). But maybe the click position matters - maybe I need to click on the exact center of the cross.
Actually, I think I need to reconsider the whole approach. Let me look at what ACTION7 does, since it's a valid action. Maybe it's the "confirm" or "apply" action.
Let me try: click on a cross to select it, then press ACTION7 to confirm.
